note: SNAPSHOT. Every number below was correct on catalog_version and is stale the moment a vendor changes a price or ships a model. Regenerating this file is the REQ-CAT-06 ritual, and two fields must be diffed per model on every regeneration because they change the request body: thinking_level_map (REQ-PROV-15 -- an entry that silently disappears turns a clamped request into a 400, and an entry that silently appears sends a level the model does not know) and cost, including the vendor of fallback-served rows (REQ-PROV-05.5 -- dropping it bills a fallback at the wrong rate, silently). Everything else in a row is a capability hint the clamp and the budget gate can survive being slightly wrong about. This catalog is NOT an allowlist: an unknown id under a known vendor clones that vendor's default_model row (REQ-CAT-03), so a model released after this snapshot works without an SDK release. Two vendor-wide facts that do not fit in a row: (1) all three vendors have moved their reasoning control from a token budget to a discrete level -- output_config.effort on Anthropic, reasoning_effort on OpenAI, thinkingLevel on Gemini. The Anthropic and OpenAI adapters emit their vendor's current field: on an anthropic row an INTEGER wire value is a budget_tokens and an effort TOKEN (low..max) is sent as output_config.effort with adaptive thinking, and a row that rejects temperature/top_p says so with compat.supports_sampling false. The google adapter sends an integer wire value as thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget and a token (MINIMAL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) as thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel, never both; a google row records the levels the vendor documents for that model as tokens and the rest as PRESENT-AND-NULL. Present-null and absent are runtime-identical (ruling P-28); the runtime effect of a fully null ladder is that the thinking parameter is omitted -- the vendor's own default, never a 400 -- and the adapter warns that the level was not expressible. An `off` entry that is present-and-null means the model cannot stop thinking and the anthropic adapter omits the key for a request of off rather than sending a rejected disable. (2) The google rows are the AI Studio deployment; Vertex AI is the same wire behind a different host and credential and is selected by configuration (Options.VertexProject or a Vertex base URL), never by a catalog row.

claude-fable-5-1.name: Claude Fable 5.1
claude-fable-5-1.note: Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled: `off` is present-and-null, so the adapter omits the thinking key ({"type":"disabled"} is a 400 here). Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; budget_tokens is rejected on this model, and so are temperature/top_p (compat.supports_sampling false drops them). Forced tool_choice any/tool is also a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Cache read is 0.025x input on this row -- a quarter of the 0.1x every other Anthropic row charges. Cache write is the 5-minute rate (1.25x input); a 1h write is priced by provider.ComputeCost, not from this row.

claude-fable-5.name: Claude Fable 5
claude-fable-5.note: Predecessor of claude-fable-5-1 at the same per-token price and the same always-on thinking: `off` is present-and-null (disabled is a 400), levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are rejected. The one billing difference is cache read at the standard 0.1x input rather than Fable 5.1's 0.025x.

claude-opus-5-5.name: Claude Opus 5.5
claude-opus-5-5.note: Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled: `off` is present-and-null, so the adapter omits the thinking key ({"type":"disabled"} is a 400, as is budget_tokens -- both probed against the API on 2026-09-30, and the migration guide says the same). Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; default effort is medium. temperature/top_p/top_k are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). Forced tool_choice any/tool is also a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Priced at $4/$20, below Opus 5's $5/$25. Cache write is the 5-minute rate ($5 = 1.25x input; 1h is $8 and is priced by provider.ComputeCost); cache read is $0.20 = 0.05x input. 1M context at one price, so no tiers. Released 2026-09-22; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-22.

claude-opus-5.name: Claude Opus 5
claude-opus-5.note: Effort-style row: every level above off is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}. Omitting the key also means adaptive on this model (thinking is on by default), and `off` is "disabled", which the model accepts only at effort high or below -- the adapter sends no effort alongside disabled, so the default (high) applies. budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s here (compat.supports_sampling false). Cache write is the 5-minute rate (1.25x input); cache read is 0.1x input.

claude-opus-4-8.name: Claude Opus 4.8
claude-opus-4-8.note: Same request surface as claude-opus-4-7: effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s. Unlike Opus 5, omitting the thinking key means NO thinking on this model, which is why every level above off must be sent explicitly as adaptive.

claude-opus-4-7.name: Claude Opus 4.7
claude-opus-4-7.note: The generation that removed budget_tokens and the sampling parameters and introduced the xhigh effort: levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", temperature/top_p are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). Omitting the thinking key means no thinking here.

claude-opus-4-6.name: Claude Opus 4.6
claude-opus-4-6.note: First adaptive-thinking generation: levels are effort tokens sent with {"type":"adaptive"} and `off` is "disabled". xhigh is ABSENT -- it arrived with Opus 4.7 -- so a request for xhigh clamps UP to max (REQ-PROV-15). budget_tokens still works but is deprecated and this adapter never sends it to an effort row; temperature/top_p are still accepted.

claude-sonnet-5-5.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
claude-sonnet-5-5.note: Adaptive thinking is on by default. `off` is "between_tools", not "disabled": {"type":"disabled"} is a 400 on this model (probed 2026-09-30) -- unlike Sonnet 5, which still accepts it. between_tools skips up-front thinking (the short updates written between tool calls still come back as thinking blocks) and is rejected by the other 5.x rows. It works only at effort high or below, and the adapter sends no effort alongside off, so the default (high) applies. Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; budget_tokens is a 400 and so is any temperature/top_p/top_k (compat.supports_sampling false). Forced tool_choice any/tool is a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Same $2/$10 and cache rates as Sonnet 5; cache write is the 5-minute rate ($2.50 = 1.25x input; 1h is $4). 1M context at one price, so no tiers. Released 2026-09-28; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-28.

claude-sonnet-5.name: Claude Sonnet 5
claude-sonnet-5.note: Vendor default_model: the clone template for unknown anthropic ids, and therefore the row an id released after this snapshot inherits its window, cap, price and effort-style ladder from. Levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). $2/$10 is the standard rate; the once-scheduled rise to $3/$15 did not happen. 1M context at one price -- no long-context tier, which is why cost.tiers is absent here and present on every openai row.

claude-sonnet-4-6.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
claude-sonnet-4-6.note: Same ladder and rules as claude-opus-4-6 one tier down: effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", no xhigh (clamps up to max), temperature/top_p accepted, budget_tokens deprecated and never sent by this adapter.

claude-opus-4-5.name: Claude Opus 4.5
claude-opus-4-5.note: Budget-wire row: the values are thinking token budgets for {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":N}, 1024 is the vendor minimum, and `off` is "disabled". xhigh and max are ABSENT, so a request for either clamps DOWN to high. 200k window and 64k output cap -- a sibling clone of the default_model would get 1M/128k and be wrong about this one. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-11-24 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.

claude-sonnet-4-5.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
claude-sonnet-4-5.note: Budget-wire row like claude-opus-4-5: token budgets, 1024 minimum, `off` is "disabled", xhigh/max absent and clamped down to high. 200k window, 64k output cap. output_config.effort is an error on this model, which is why the ladder is budgets and not tokens. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-09-29 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.

claude-haiku-4-5.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
claude-haiku-4-5.note: The smallest current row and a budget-wire one: the values are thinking token budgets, 1024 is the vendor minimum, `off` is "disabled". xhigh and max are ABSENT rather than null -- nothing was checked, they are opt-in -- so a request for max clamps DOWN to high, REQ-PROV-15's worked example. 200k window and 64k cap; output_config.effort is an error here, so the ladder stays in budgets. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-10-15 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.
